subject: DPA: data communication obligations and subprocessor export policy

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@brightbank.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Clarifying DPA communication windows and subprocessor export expectations

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the DPA draft. A couple of quick clarifying questions from our side before we route redlines to Legal:

1) Notification cadence: BrightBank's draft currently requires "prompt notice" for security events and a "final report within 72 hours." For production incidents that materially affect customer data, can you confirm whether you need a separate timely ACK (i.e., acknowledgement of receipt) vs. the substantive report?

2) Subprocessor exports: the contract language implies BrightBank may request full forensic exports (including raw export of PII) from subprocessors. We want to understand practical constraints: cross-border export restrictions (EU -> US), customer-specific redaction requirements, and whether you expect the full disk image or a curated forensic package.

We want to offer workable commitments: an acknowledgement within a narrow window plus staged deliverables (initial triage, then fuller forensic package). Before I propose working language, looping in Markus and Irene on operational/legal feasibility.

Short on time today — suggested path: if BrightBank is OK with an initial ACK within 4 hours of detection, an initial triage summary within 24 hours, and a complete export package (where permitted) within 96 hours for high-severity events, we can accept that with explicit carveouts for jurisdictions with export controls. If that sounds off, tell us your priority and we will adapt.

Thanks,

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Vanessa —

Thank you. A couple of clarifications from our legal/compliance side:

- Acknowledgement vs report: we require an acknowledgement that the incident has been received and triaged within 24 hours, but for critical incidents (we define critical as confirmed exfiltration of customer data) we prefer an ACK within 12 hours.
- Full forensic package: our standard position is we need a complete forensic package within 48 hours for critical incidents to meet our regulator reporting timelines. We appreciate the export control concerns; in places with explicit export restrictions we'll accept a metadata-first approach plus a plan for curated evidence transfer contingent on lawful basis.

Two asks for Redwood:
1) Please confirm whether Redwood can provide — on request — a list of active subprocessors engaged for BrightBank's tenant within 24 hours.
2) Can Redwood commit to daily status updates until the issue is resolved for incidents that meet the "critical" threshold?

If you can send proposed clause text today, our legal team will do a quick pass.

Best,
Alice Nguyen
Senior Counsel, Data Protection
BrightBank

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@brightbank.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarifying DPA communication windows and subprocessor export expectations

Alice —

Thanks for the clear priorities. Operationally, here's what we can realistically accept and commit to without creating undue risk or breaching third-party obligations:

- Severity buckets: we'll propose contract language that defines "critical" (confirmed exfiltration or unauthorized export of customer PII), "high" (large-scope disruption with possible data exposure), and "medium/low."
- Windows: proposed compromise — acknowledgement within 12 hours for critical (24 hours for high), initial triage summary within 24 hours for critical incidents (48 hours for high), and a curated forensic package within 96 hours where legally permitted. We can accelerate to 48 hours for curated package only under pre-agreed SOC/contract terms and dedicated resource allocation (we can discuss a premium response SLA separately).
- Subprocessor roster: we can provide an up-to-date list of subprocessors for BrightBank's instance within 24 hours of request (we already maintain this data). For forensic exports, we need the customer's explicit written request and acceptance of any export/export-control constraints.

Operational asks back to BrightBank: daily status updates until remediation is complete for critical incidents; a point-of-contact who can sign off on any cross-border evidence transfer approvals; and explicit scope of what you need in the forensic package (log slice, KV caches, full payloads).

Irene: could you confirm the legal framing we should propose? I'll draft redline language reflecting the windows above and the export-carveouts./MK

--
Markus Klein
Director, Platform Security & Ops
Redwood Inference

Hi Alice / team —

Following Markus' operational note, attaching a redline (dpa_clause_redline_vortiz_20261130.docx) and a short forensic guidance doc (forensic_export_guidance_v1.pdf). High-level recommended contract language below — this is meant to be a tight but practical compromise that addresses regulator timing while protecting against unlawful transfer obligations: 

1) Definitions:
- "Critical Incident": confirmed unauthorized exfiltration of customer data or unauthorized disclosure to an unaffiliated third party.
- "Forensic Package": curated data extract including (a) relevant system logs, (b) routing/metadata, (c) KV cache slices and (d) any customer-requested payloads subject to export controls.

2) Notification & Deliverables:
- Acknowledgement: Redwood will provide an initial acknowledgement of receipt within 12 hours of detection for Critical Incidents (24 hours for High).
- Initial triage summary: Redwood will provide a written triage summary within 24 hours for Critical Incidents (48 hours for High), including scope, affected tenants, and immediate mitigation steps taken.
- Forensic package: Where permitted by applicable law, Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to deliver the Forensic Package within 96 hours for Critical Incidents. Where the customer requires a 48-hour delivery timeline for a curated package, both parties will execute a pre-agreed emergency support addendum covering resource mobilization and potential costs.

3) Subprocessors & Exports:
- Subprocessor inventory: Redwood will provide an up-to-date list of subprocessors engaged for the customer's tenant upon request within 24 hours.
- Export constraints: For jurisdictions with applicable export restrictions, Redwood will provide a metadata-first package and a documented transfer plan. Transfers of raw payloads that would contravene local law will require the customer's written consent and any necessary lawful-basis documentation.

4) Cooperation & Status Updates:
- Redwood will provide daily status updates until closure for Critical Incidents and will escalate to an agreed executive sponsor if remediation extends beyond 14 days.
- Customer may request additional artifacts; Redwood will respond to such requests within 48 hours and, where necessary, provide a timeline and effort estimate for fulfilment.

5) Audit & Escrow:
- Where the customer has pre-requested escrow or forensic-handover arrangements (e.g., encrypted snapshots to a customer-controlled escrow), Redwood will comply per the executed addendum.

If that is OK from BrightBank's perspective, Suzanne in Legal who is cc'd on the redline can do a narrow pass to ensure the language aligns with our broader DPA template.

Thanks — attaching the two files for convenience.

Irene Choi
Deputy GC, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
